title: Pair With Target Sum
problem: The first line is a positive integer N. The second line holds N integers separated by spaces. The third line holds a target T. Print "Yes" if two numbers at different positions in the list add up to T, and "No" otherwise. A number can't be paired with itself, but two equal numbers at different positions can. For example, in 1 4 6 the pair 4 + 6 makes 10, so for T = 10 the answer is Yes.
starter_code:
# The first line is N, the second line holds N integers,
# the third line holds the target T.
# Print "Yes" if two different positions add up to T, otherwise "No".

# Write your code here

hints.1: For each number, think about which other number it would need to reach the target.
hints.2: Loop over the numbers, keeping a set of the numbers seen so far. For each number x, if T - x is already in the set, a pair exists; then add x to the set. Checking the set before adding x stops a number from pairing with itself.
hints.3:
input()
nums = list(map(int, input().split()))
t = int(input())
seen = set()
found = False
for x in nums:
    if t - x in seen:
        found = True
    seen.add(x)
print('Yes' if found else 'No')

failure_explanation: The two numbers must come from different positions: one number on its own is not a pair, even if doubling it reaches the target. Two equal numbers at different positions do count. Print the words exactly as shown.
